title: Finding the Range of a Shifted Hyperbolic Radical Function
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the range of the real-valued function defined by y = 2 + sqrt(9 + x^2).

steps.title: Bound the Quadratic Radicand from Below
steps.explanation: Since x^2 >= 0 for all real numbers x, the quantity 9 + x^2 is always at least 9, achieving its minimum value 9 at x = 0.
steps.why: Squares of real numbers are non-negative, with minimum 0 at x = 0.

steps.title: Apply the Principal Square Root
steps.explanation: Because the principal square root function is strictly increasing on [0, inf), 9 + x^2 >= 9 implies sqrt(9 + x^2) >= 3.
steps.why: Applying a monotonically increasing function to both sides of an inequality preserves the inequality.

steps.title: Add the Constant Shift and State the Range
steps.explanation: Adding 2 gives y >= 5, with y(0) = 5. As |x| -> infinity, sqrt(9 + x^2) grows without bound, so by continuity y attains every real number in [5, inf).
steps.why: A continuous function that attains a global minimum of 5 and grows without bound has range [5, inf).
